external_dictionary_review.notes: Generation-stage senses use the repository lexicon; independent lexical approval remains separate.

freshness_method: Guarded promotion checks selected target IDs against canonical Urdu A1, A2, and B1 sequences 1-48 immediately before append.

targets.intended_sense: mayor; local civic executive or chair in the fictional scenario
a crowd or large gathered group
a rule, regulation, or formal procedure
registration or formal recording of an application or exception
a limited concession or allowance within a rule
a party or stakeholder affected by a public choice
justice or fairness in treatment and process
citizenship, with emphasis on responsible participation in public life
unfair exploitation of another person's vulnerable position
a bribe or improper benefit intended to influence an official decision
a short public slogan used to express or mobilize support for a cause
growth or increase, here of housing/population
neighboring or adjacent area/person; here an adjacent district

generation_guardrails: P1-P5 introduce exactly three new targets each; P6 introduces none and visibly recycles all fifteen.
All scenarios are fictional/local-process examples and do not assert current political facts or advocate a party or ideology.
Bribery and exploitation are explained as governance/transparency concepts without facilitating wrongdoing.
All six passages retain ten questions and ten linked answers and remain within the 220-320 whitespace-token B1 band.
Learner-facing title, passage text, questions, and answers use Urdu script only.
Guarded promotion fails closed on target freshness, schema drift, QA links, script leakage, first-introduction collisions, or state mismatch.
Generation/integrity state remains separate from educator/publication release approval.
freshness_scope: Exact target IDs checked against all canonical Urdu A1, A2, and B1 sequences 1-48 immediately before Unit 9 append.
